question.text: A PM wants to add one more security to her 10-asset portfolio. She evaluates 4 candidates with correlations 0.0, 0.25, -0.35, -0.85 vs the existing portfolio. For MAXIMUM risk-reduction via diversification, she should pick:

explanation.text: The Logic: Most negative correlation = greatest diversification benefit. ρ = -0.85 offers near-perfect offset — ideal candidate. The Trap: Students confused by 'lower absolute correlation'; diversification works best with lowest (most negative) correlation. Cross-Exam Context: MPT application. Manager's Pro-Tip: Real negative correlations are rare — gold, puts, and certain defensive assets are typical sources.
